title: The Geometry of LLM-as-Judge: Why Inter-LLM Consensus Is Not Human Alignment

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the geometric misalignment (principal angle) between LLM score subspaces and human score subspaces on subjective, culturally situated rubrics across Indic languages.
Evaluating variations in geometric signatures, such as principal angle and score spread, across eight different Indic languages to compare high-resource versus low-resource language performance.
Analyzing the collapse of LLM judges into low-rank projectors that prioritize model-legible directions (like response length) over human-aligned quality manifolds.
Identifying how LLM judges prioritize surface-level corpus patterns over multidimensional human evaluation criteria in subjective tasks.
